## Summary

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Python 3.10+ managed with `uv`  
**Primary Dependencies**: aiogram 3.x, SQLAlchemy 2.0, Pydantic, Loguru, async HTTP client (`httpx` preferred; justify if using `aiohttp`)  
**Storage**: SQLite (`data/szgmu_bot.db`) via SQLAlchemy models in `app/database/`  
**Testing**: `pytest` with async support, project markers (`unit`, `integration`, `slow`, `database`, `external`)  
**Target Platform**: Telegram bot running on Linux container/VM with scheduled background tasks  
**Project Type**: Asynchronous bot + service layer  
**Performance Goals**: Schedule responses < 3s for cached groups, exports generated within 5s, notifications delivered within configured window  
**Constraints**: No blocking I/O in handlers, canonical data lives in database, secrets pulled from `.env` only  
**Scale/Scope**: SZGMU student body (tens of thousands of users) with daily schedule queries and periodic exports

## Constitution Check

*GATE: You MUST validate every item below before Phase 0 research completes and re-affirm before implementation.*

- [ ] **Principle I – Canonical Schedule Data Discipline**: Explain how schedule ingestion, storage, and exports remain aligned. Call out any migrations or seeding impacts.
- [ ] **Principle II – Async Telegram Orchestration**: Detail handler ↔ service interactions, chosen async clients, and how background jobs reuse services without duplicating logic.
- [ ] **Principle III – Student Value First**: Describe copy, localization, and profile preference touch points. Note how error states guide students back to success.
- [ ] **Principle IV – Tests Before Code**: List the failing tests you will author first (unit/integration) and where they live. Identify markers and fixtures required.
- [ ] **Principle V – Operational Transparency & Resilience**: Outline logging, observability, and failure-handling expectations (timeouts, retries, alerts) for this feature.

Any deliberate divergence requires a Complexity Tracking entry before Phase 1 begins.
